Using a keyboard with NoCharge browser games

Keyboard input varies by NoCharge game. Learn the standard button path, examples of title-specific keys, and why this overview is not a blanket accessibility certification.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Check the current platform.

Use the public pages behind this explanation.

Open the ArcadeReview PrivacyKeyboard-only play notes

Bottom line: Keyboard controls vary by game. Many V2 interactions use native buttons, selects, and text inputs; only some titles add arrow keys or letter shortcuts. Check the current game page instead of assuming a universal control scheme.

Start with the controls on the page

Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move among focusable controls. Enter or Space activates a focused button; native selects and text fields use their usual browser behavior. This is useful for games whose board cells, move buttons, and coordinate selectors are ordinary controls.

Examples of title-specific input

  • Twenty Forty-Eight: focus the board and use arrow keys or W, A, S, D; directional buttons are also available.
  • Lights Out: arrow keys move focus among the 5×5 buttons; Enter or Space presses the focused square.
  • Hangman: during an active round, A–Z keys submit guesses when focus is not in a text input; letter buttons are also present.
  • Beacon Lattice, Minesweeper, Nonogram, Word Search, and Sudoku: use the page’s labeled buttons and, where shown, row/column selectors. The current source does not expose the old number-key, F/X, chord, or universal arrow shortcuts described in earlier copy.

Pass the Picture has a boundary

The shared drawing surface supports pointer, pen, or touch input for freehand strokes. A keyboard user can use the Add a sample line button as an alternate contribution, but that is not keyboard control of arbitrary freehand drawing.

Do not overread this list

This page does not claim that 23 of 24 games are “keyboard-complete,” and NoCharge does not publish a current all-games keyboard-completeness percentage. A native control path is not a certification for every assistive technology, keyboard layout, browser, or operating system. Manual testing remains separate from code inspection.

A practical check

On the live game page, use Tab to reach the first game control, activate it, complete a move, and confirm that focus remains visible and the status is understandable. Then check reset, pause, and any game-specific key on that page. If a path is not documented there, do not assume it exists.
